Consult Summary:
- 28-year-old female with new-onset left-sided posterior throbbing headache since yesterday; no red flag symptoms reported; advised analgesia escalation, hydration/rest, and safety-net follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began yesterday mid-morning; gradual build over a short period; persistent; not time-of-day dependent.
- Location/character/severity: Left occipital region; throbbing, intense; 8/10 severity.
- Associated symptoms: Denies nausea, vomiting, tingling, numbness, weakness, blurred vision, eye pain, visual aura/“funny lights,” photophobia, fever, chills, sweats, rash. Eating/drinking normal. Slept through night.
- Pertinent negatives: No positional worsening (lying, standing, bending), no cough/sneeze exacerbation. No prior similar headaches (“not really”).
- Past medical history: None reported. No asthma or stomach problems.
- Medications: None reported routinely.
- OTC/Trialed: Ibuprofen (Nurofen) taken yesterday without relief.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Family history: Mother with hypertension and migraines.
- Social history: Lives with partner. Occupation: Designer. No tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drug use. Has not missed work but reports difficulty performing normal activities due to headache.
- Preventive care: Blood pressure not checked recently.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical exam: Not documented.

Impression:
- Acute left-sided headache without red flag features; etiology not specified in transcript.

Plan:
- Analgesia: Start a “slightly stronger” NSAID alternative to ibuprofen, to be taken instead of ibuprofen and regularly with food (medication name and dose/route/frequency not documented). May take paracetamol (acetaminophen) concurrently.
- Self-care: Rest and maintain good hydration.
- Safety-net: Seek care if pain worsens or if new symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness) or if recurrent episodes occur.
- Follow-up: If not improving within 1–2 days after starting the prescribed medication, contact the clinic; prescription to be collected from pharmacy.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergy status; pregnancy status; current medication reconciliation; vitals and blood pressure; neurological examination; name and dosing details of prescribed analgesic.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall with minor pauses; no significant audio issues.
